classification.difficultyReason: Students complete the scaffolded annual balance updates, compare the final balance with the car price, and interpret the difference as money remaining. Five years and a decimal rate add calculation without introducing a new strategy.

content.prompt: Alison invests $\$7890$ at 8.9% p.a. compound interest for 5 years.

inlines.text: Complete the table to find the final value at the end of 5 years. Keep full precision in intermediate calculations and round the final value to 2 decimal places.
Each ending balance becomes the next starting balance. Interest = starting balance × 8.9%. Display amounts to cents and retain unrounded values in intermediate calculations.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Will she have enough to buy a car worth $\$12000$? If so, by how much?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Amount remaining}&=12084.15819373650261-12000\\\text{Amount remaining}&=84.15819373650261\end{align*}$$
Yes. Her final balance exceeds $\$12\,000$, leaving $\$84.16$ to 2 decimal places.
